title: Ops micro-announcement template + QA (scratch)
content:
Note to self: quick, scannable micro-announce template for small operational changes (throttle/window/billing grace). Keep it <60 words for Slack + 1-paragraph email variant + 3 FAQs. Purpose: reduce back-and-forth, provide durable link, and enable oncall to paste and go.

1) Intended audience
- Primary: internal engineers (SRE, infra, serving-runtime)
- Secondary: CSM for any customer-facing escalation; product owners if changes affect contracts

2) When to use
- Transient capacity constraints (non-severe) where an explicit temporary tweak is made: e.g., embedding throughput reduced for 45m, small quota soft-limits, scheduled small-scale rollbacks, planned maintenance windows under 2 hours.

3) Micro-announcement template (Slack-friendly) - one line headline + link
- HEADLINE: [Ops] Short description — Impact summary (duration)
- BODY (optional): 1 sentence with who is impacted and any immediate mitigation (fallback model/route)
- CTA: link to incident doc or playbook and mention oncall rotation (e.g., @oncall)

Example (Slack paste):
[Ops] Brief embedding throttle — reduced embeddings throughput for EU region (45m). Affects large batch jobs only; low-latency API traffic unaffected. Fallback: cached prefixes enabled. Details & status: <link> @oncall

4) Email/All-team blurb (short paragraph variant)
- Subject: Ops: temporary throughput adjustment in EU region (45m window)
- Body: We applied a temporary throughput reduction to embeddings in the EU region to stabilize a hotspot on gpu-pool-3. This affects large batch embedding jobs (>=1000 items) but not typical request traffic or dedicated customers on Reserved pools. We expect normal service to resume at ~15:35 UTC. Follow the incident doc for live updates: <link>. Reach out on Slack #platform-ops for urgent issues.

5) Talking points for quick standup/all-hands (30–60s)
- What happened: brief causal phrase (e.g., "hotspot during backfill")
- Impact: who was affected (scale + latency or availability)
- Action taken: mitigation and timeline
- Next steps: follow-up (postmortem owners, CS outreach if needed)

6) Short Q&A (3–5 questions) - answer in 1–2 lines each
Q: Will customers see errors?
A: No increased 5xx expected for API traffic; large batch jobs will be rate-limited and see delayed progress. Dedicated customers unaffected unless specifically on the impacted node.

Q: Does this change billing or quotas?
A: No immediate billing changes; if we extend throttles beyond the promised window, we will inform CS and consider goodwill credits per policy.

Q: Who do I ping for urgent unblock?
A: @oncall on #platform-ops; if no response in 10m escalate to the SRE lead (Ravi Menon).

Q: Is this related to the recent quantization rollout?
A: No, separate. This was a capacity hotspot on gpu-pool-3 triggered by an unexpected backfill.

7) Checklist before posting micro-announce (quick, 6 items)
- [ ] Confirm duration estimate with SRE owner
- [ ] Verify mitigation/fallback is in place (cache/burst route)
- [ ] Create slip doc or incident stub with link
- [ ] Add oncall mention and escalation path in message
- [ ] Notify CS if any customers are known to be impacted (list short IDs)
- [ ] Draft short follow-up note for 1-hour status update

8) Open questions / TODOs for this template (notes to self)
- Decide if we should include a short "expected user-visible symptoms" line by default (makes copy longer).
- Should micro-announcements be auto-scheduled into status page or only manual? Ops prefers manual unless severity high. Need product stake.
- Add quick fields to incident stub: severity, mitigation, estimated recovery, affected components. Can we reuse ops-playbook incident schema? (see linked PR)

9) Tone guide (for the message) - 3 bullets to keep consistent
- Direct, technical, non-alarming: convey impact without hyperbole
- Action-first: what we did, what we will do, how to get help
- Short: treat as operational patch notes, not a narrative

10) Quick rehearsal notes (for use in a rapid standup if asked live)
- "We saw a localized hotspot on gpu-pool-3 during a large batch backfill. We reduced throughput to stabilize the node, which will delay large embedding jobs for about 45 minutes. API traffic is unaffected. We're monitoring and will post another update in 1 hour."

11) Copybank (snippets to paste)
- Headline: [Ops] {brief} — {impact} ({duration})
- One-line status: Stabilized; monitoring.
- Escalation: Ping @oncall on #platform-ops; escalate to SRE lead if no response in 10m.

12) Postmortem trigger guidance (short)
- Trigger a blameless postmortem if: any customer-experienced errors, if outage >1 hour, or if rollback required. Otherwise add as incident note with retrospective items in sprint retro.

13) Logistics for storage + discoverability
- Keep one canonical micro-announcements folder on Confluence (linked above). Consider an index page with 30-day archive and quick filters.

Final note: keep this intentionally lightweight. The goal is fast, repeatable messaging that engineering oncall can send with minimal editing. Next steps: iterate with Ravi + CS for wording, then add small template macro to Slack shortcuts.

-- Saffron (scratchpad)
